text:
Theo: heads-up: found a subtle parity bug between the Go SDK and REST for generation params. SDK serializes `maxTokens` (camelCase) but our API expects `max_tokens` (snake_case). server ignores unknown camelCase fields and falls back to default max_tokens=512, causing unexpected truncation in a few jobs.

Priya: ouch. repro?

Theo: minimal repro (go-sdk v0.9.3):

```go
// SDK usage
client.Generate(ctx, GenerateParams{MaxTokens: 1024, Prompt: "..."})
// SDK sends JSON body: {"prompt":"...","maxTokens":1024}
// server treats it as {"prompt":"..."} -> default max_tokens=512
```

Theo: direct curl with server-style field works as expected:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":1024}'
# -> respects 1024
```

Jamie: that explains the truncation reports we saw in QA. SDK should map field names to the wire format we expect. did the Go marshaller auto-transform fields historically?

Lina: looks like a recent refactor to idiomatic Go structs removed explicit JSON tags for some fields, so `MaxTokens int `json:"max_tokens"`` was lost and now defaults to Go field name -> camelCase.

Priya: workaround for now: set the param via raw body or call REST directly, but we should fix the SDK.

Jamie: agreed. plan: 1) add missing json tags for all public params to match API snake_case, 2) add unit tests that marshal structs and assert exact wire keys, 3) add an integration test that sends `max_tokens` and asserts server behavior. I'll open RED-5602 and a draft PR.

Theo: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-go-sdk/pull/204 (draft). also add a lint rule to fail CI if exported fields are missing json tags for public request structs.

Lina: good call on lint rule. also audit other language SDKs for similar regressions (TS/py may be fine but worth checking).

devops-bot: Created issue RED-5602: "Go SDK: ensure JSON field names use snake_case to match API" assigned to @Jamie.

Jamie: target: patch release 0.9.4 tomorrow morning, include migration note (rare: callers using custom raw marshalling might be affected). no objections?

Priya: none. will update QA tests to catch this during canary.

Theo: thanks all :thumbsup:
